v3 parameters (reports/f1-qualification-spec-v3-2026-10.md): valuation > $1B is the gate; headcount 51+; capacity ~$2.5M/yr (not in distress); no F1 tie direct or via parent; not sanctioned. Verdicts: Yes (blue) = passes, fit >= 2, credible marketing motive. Stretch (amber) = passes with one real reservation. Low-value (RED) = passes the gates but judged a waste of time (fit 0-1, pre-revenue with no marketing function, concentrated B2B supplier, or state entity with no consumer brand). No = failed a gate -> 99 REJECTS. Column A on every tab (also_on_tabs) lists the summary tabs the same brand also sits on: 01 PRIORITY, 02 UP-AND-COMING and/or 03 FUNDED $100M+. Solid red = the brand is on the priority list (brand name also in red); amber = on 02 and/or 03 only; blank = on this tab only. So a red or amber row is a repeat of a brand you have already seen on a summary tab, not an extra prospect.

Priority score: Yes 60+fit*8, Stretch 40+fit*6, Low-value 20+fit*4. Each tab ranks best first. Tab 01 PRIORITY lists every main-list Yes across all sectors, ranked best first: start outreach there. up_and_coming = crossed $1B within 24 months, growing >40%/yr, 2025-26 IPO, visible challenger, or announced new-market entry (shown on tab 02). Track F names sit on tab 03 and the F-prefixed tabs.

Source pools: G = broad discovery sweep across all sectors and regions; A = v2 reject recovered because it failed only on a removed test; B = unicorn-register name now eligible without the revenue bar; F = Track F (funded USD 100M+, below USD 1B valuation), shown on F-prefixed tabs and the consolidated FUNDED tab.
